drafts.title: Voice assistant reliably executes common driving commands
drafts.description: While driving, customers can speak common navigation, climate and media commands and the car executes them reliably without needing to repeat or correct the command.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a real-driving noise test (urban and highway noise profiles) the voice assistant correctly recognizes and executes at least 95% of a standardized set of 50 common driving commands (navigation destination entry, call control, media control, climate setpoints) within 3 seconds.
assumptions: Test languages: English (US) and other major languages for the market tested.
Cellular connectivity is available for cloud-based recognition where applicable; offline recognition may be used as fallback.
The standardized command set is representative of top 50 customer voice intents.
uncertainties: Voice recognition performance may vary with aftermarket windshield coatings, heavy accents, or severe background noise (worksites).
Some improvements may rely on cloud models and therefore on connectivity.

drafts.title: Wireless charging maintains uninterrupted charging for common phones
drafts.description: When a customer places a compatible phone on the in‑car wireless pad during a drive, charging continues reliably and does not stop unexpectedly.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across 10 representative phone models (including popular iOS and Android models) and common thin protective cases (<=3 mm), the charging pad sustains charging without interruption in at least 95% of 30‑minute driving sessions in vehicle vibration and temperature conditions.
assumptions: Phones tested are running manufacturer-approved wireless charging firmware and support the Qi standard.
Typical protective cases are <=3 mm thickness and do not contain metal.
Interference from aftermarket accessories is not included in the baseline test.
uncertainties: Some phone models or firmware updates may reduce compatibility after vehicle launch.
MagSafe-style alignment requirements for some phones may affect results.

drafts.title: HUD and center display remain legible in bright sunlight and glare
drafts.description: Customers can read primary driving information and glance information on the head‑up display and read key content on the center screen when driving in bright sunlight without struggling with glare.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a daylight glare usability test (sun angle and luminance representative of direct sunlight), at least 90% of test participants can correctly read primary HUD content (speed, next navigation cue) within 1.5 seconds and at least 90% can read key center‑screen driving/navigation information within 2.5 seconds from the normal driving seating position.
assumptions: Test uses standardized lighting rigs that simulate direct sun at typical driving angles.
Participants use normal daytime eyewear (sunglasses included) representative of the market.
HUD and screen brightness controls are set to automatic and allowed to increase to their design maximum for the test.
uncertainties: Extreme aftermarket window tint or polarized sunglasses may still affect legibility.
Absolute luminance achievable by displays may be constrained by power/thermal tradeoffs.

drafts.title: Tactile climate controls for eyes‑free adjustments
drafts.description: Customers can adjust cabin temperature and fan speed by touch without needing to look at the screen, using tactile controls that are intuitive to find from the driving position.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a blind (eyes-occluded) user test, 90% of participants can change cabin temperature by ±2°C and change fan speed by one level within 3 seconds by touch alone.
assumptions: Tests are performed from the standard driver seating position and with typical driving gloves not thicker than 2 mm.
Controls use tactile differences (shape, surface, haptic feedback) that are discoverable by touch.
uncertainties: Extreme glove thickness or unusual hand sizes may change results.
Some climate features may remain on-screen for advanced configuration; only primary temperature and fan must be accessible by touch.

drafts.title: Cold‑weather package includes heated steering wheel and is clearly represented in configurator
drafts.description: Customers can choose a Cold‑Weather package that includes a heated steering wheel (no separate mandatory option) and see clearly in the online configurator and at dealerships that the steering wheel is included in that package.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The Cold‑Weather package includes the heated steering wheel for all listed trims in the US configurator and dealer documentation; 100% of configurator builds that include Cold‑Weather package show the heated steering wheel as included without additional separate option.
assumptions: This requirement applies to the US market for the successor vehicle launch.
Dealer ordering system and online configurator are synchronized to show package contents.
uncertainties: Regional regulatory or homologation differences may affect feature availability in other markets.
Some limited edition or performance trims may have different package structures.

drafts.title: Transparent configurator and option/subscription management in car and app
drafts.description: Customers can configure the vehicle with clear, itemized information about which options are one‑time purchases, which are subscriptions, and see an estimated monthly payment for a standard finance or lease term so they can compare total cost and option inclusion without confusion.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The online/configurator flow displays an itemized cost line for every optional package and accessory, flags subscriptions distinctly, and provides an estimated monthly payment for a 36‑month lease or 60‑month finance plan; in a usability study 90% of participants rate the configurator as 'clear' (Likert 4/5 or higher) for option and cost transparency. Subscription options can be activated from the in‑car UI or companion app within two user actions.
assumptions: Monthly payment estimates assume a configurable down payment and a defined credit term (36-month lease, 60-month finance) and are clearly marked as estimates.
Subscription activation requires account authentication in the app or vehicle and available payment method.
Competitor lease comparisons are provided as an optional view but are not mandated as part of the core configurator.
uncertainties: Local tax, fees and dealer incentives can change the final monthly payment and may differ from the displayed estimate.
Third-party subscription payment processors and varying regional regulations may affect activation flows.

drafts.title: CCC (China) infotainment certification request (informational, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers request that the infotainment system passes China Compulsory Certification (CCC) for sales in the Chinese market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured as a regulatory requirement for legal/market teams; engineering acceptance criteria and certification activities to be defined by regulatory program.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification/regulatory requirements are out of scope for product feature requirements; logged for legal and homologation teams.

drafts.title: GDPR compliance for driver profile (informational, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that their stored driver profiles satisfy GDPR data storage and deletion requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured as a privacy/legal requirement to be fulfilled by legal and backend teams; implementation details and acceptance tests owned by compliance.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation and legal compliance are out of scope for product requirement drafts; logged for privacy/compliance owners.

drafts.title: Requested cockpit chip (Snapdragon 8295) (engineering spec, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers specifically asked that the cockpit computer use the Snapdragon 8295 chip.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is an engineering component request; platform and supplier decisions are handled by engineering and procurement.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component/part requests are engineering specifications and out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafts; logged for engineering consideration.

drafts.title: Base price target below $50,000 (pricing/business case, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the base price be lowered below 50,000 USD.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured as a pricing/business request for product planning and finance; detailed pricing decisions are out of scope for product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Pricing and business-case targets are out of scope for product requirements; logged for pricing/strategy teams.

drafts.title: Competitively cheaper lease than Mercedes (pricing request, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers requested a monthly lease rate cheaper than the Mercedes competitor.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured for pricing and competitive strategy teams to evaluate; not a product technical requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Lease price positioning is a business/pricing decision and out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request to include all options in base price (pricing/business case, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that all option packages be included at no extra charge in the base price.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured as a pricing/packaging request for commercial teams; not implemented as a product technical requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Broad pricing model changes are out of scope for product requirements; logged for commercial/strategy teams.

drafts.title: Request to reduce Comfort package cost by 30% (pricing/business case, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the Comfort package be discounted by 30 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured for pricing and commercial evaluation; product requirements will reflect package contents but not mandated price changes.
drafts.scope_reason: Package pricing is a commercial decision and out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Request to lower dealer margin on optional extras (business/pricing, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that dealers earn a lower margin on optional extras.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured for distribution and commercial teams; not a product feature requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Dealer margin and commercial agreements are out of scope for product requirement drafts.

drafts.title: Requested subscription price for heated seats at $15/month (pricing request, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that heated seats be offered as a subscription at 15 USD per month.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured as a pricing suggestion for subscription product and commercial teams; exact subscription pricing is out of scope for product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific subscription price points are commercial decisions and out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Request for 0% financing offer (pricing/finance, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW offers 0 percent financing on the new model.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Captured for finance and commercial teams to evaluate; financing offers are out of scope for product functional requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Financing offers and promotional rates are commercial decisions and out of scope for product requirements.
